# Act as validator and issue after validation

When your accreditation lets you validate others (an ecosystem root, a grantor, or an issuer onboarding holders), applicants' agents connect to yours. Your backend, or an operator in the frontend, decides; the agent carries the protocol and the transaction.

## The flow from your side

| Flow state | Meaning | Your action |
|---|---|---|
| `AWAITING_OR` | An applicant's pending entry names you; its request has not arrived or was rejected | Wait |
| `VALIDATING` | The request arrived; the agent verified the applicant is who the registry says | Review |
| `OOB_PENDING` | You sent a link; the applicant is completing it | Wait, then `start-validation` |
| `VALIDATED_PENDING_CLAIMS` | Role holder, entry validated, claims missing or invalid | Edit the claims, validate again |
| `AWAITING_VALIDATION_TX` | The agent has no authorization to sign the validation | An operator signs it in the frontend |
| `COMPLETED` | Credential issued (holder role) | Done |

## Steps

```bash
# what is waiting
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/v2/vt/flows?role=validator | jq '.items[] | {participantSessionId, flowState, applicantDid}'

# send the applicant to your evidence portal
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/v2/vt/flows/<id>/oob-link -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"url":"https://portal.example.com/apply/abc","description":"Upload your registration certificate","expiresAt":"2026-11-01T00:00:00Z"}'

# when the evidence is in, resume
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/v2/vt/flows/<id>/start-validation

# for a holder: set the claims of the credential you will issue
curl -s -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:3000/v2/vt/flows/<id>/claims -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"claims":{"memberName":"Jane Doe","memberId":"M-1234"}}'

# validate: fees for the applicant's future operations, optional end date
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/v2/vt/flows/<id>/validate -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"issuanceFees":0,"verificationFees":0,"effectiveUntil":"2027-10-01T00:00:00Z"}'

# or refuse
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/v2/vt/flows/<id>/reject -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"code":"vt-flow.validation-refused","description":"The certificate does not match the applicant."}'
```

`validate` has the agent sign the on-chain validation when its VS operator authorization covers it; otherwise the flow waits in `AWAITING_VALIDATION_TX` for an operator, who finds it in the frontend's **Pending tasks**. For a holder role the agent then issues the credential over the connection.

## In the frontend

Pending tasks lists the same applications grouped by ecosystem and schema, with the applicant's Proof-of-Trust, and offers the on-chain actions (validate with fees and end date, cancel). Evidence collected by your agent or your portal is not shown there; the frontend shows what is on chain.

## Later

You can revoke the holder's entry from the frontend; the applicant's agent receives the update and removes the credential. You can issue an updated credential on the still-open connection.
